principles.rule: Use the ontology as the governing standard for adjudication.
principles.note: Pathway labels and lexical cues must not override explicit ontology criteria.

principles.rule: Select Pass A or Pass B for each record according to which pass best aligns with the ontology and the record evidence.
principles.note: Do not systematically prefer either pass.

principles.rule: Resolve the actual A/B conflict only. Preserve assignments on which both passes agree unless there is a substantial ontology error.
principles.substantial_error_definition: A shared assignment clearly violates an ontology exclusion rule, clearly fails the ontology inclusion/definition criteria, or a clearly required shared role/pathway is materially misclassified.
principles.action_if_substantial_error: Correct the shared assignment and document the ontology-based reason explicitly.

principles.rule: Do not assign topics from title alone.
principles.action_if_abstract_or_full_text_unavaila: Set adjudication status to needs_more_information or unresolved and require additional evidence.

principles.rule: Assign PRIMARY to central research questions, interventions, exposures, outcomes or conclusions; assign SECONDARY only to independently substantive but non-central topics.
principles.note: Do not use SECONDARY for background, context or incidental measurements.

principles.rule: Preserve original Pass A and Pass B outputs, final adjudication, rationale, evidence status, and any ontology-based override.
Prioritise data integrity, provenance, verifiability and reproducibility over speed unless explicitly instructed otherwise.
